title: Question 10
stem:
In an X-ray tube, electrons are accelerated through a potential difference of 75 kV. The electrons then strike a tungsten target of effective mass 15 g.
The electron energy is converted into the energy of X-ray photons with an efficiency of 5.0%. The rest of the energy is converted into thermal energy.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The X-ray tube produces an image using a current of $0.40\text{ A}$ for a time of $20\text{ ms}$.
The specific heat capacity of tungsten is $130\text{ J kg}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$.
Determine the temperature rise $\Delta T$ of the tungsten target.
$$\Delta T = \text{...................................................... K}$$
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in ideal gas laws and thermodynamics connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Ideal gas laws and thermodynamics. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
energy = mc T Δ; energy = ItV 0.40 0.020 75 000 0.95 ( T =) 0.015 130 × × × Δ ×; =290 K
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.text:
The linear attenuation coefficient of the X-ray photons in muscle is $0.22\text{ cm}^{-1}$.
Calculate the thickness $t$ of muscle that will absorb $80\%$ of the incident X-ray intensity.
$$t = \text{.................................................... cm}$$

hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in quantum physics and photoelectric effect connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Table 10.1 shows the linear attenuation coefficient $\mu$ for the X-ray photons in different tissues.
Two X-ray images are taken, one of equal thicknesses of bone and muscle and another of equal thicknesses of blood and muscle.
Explain why one of these images has good contrast, but the other does not.

markscheme_points.text: either (linear) attenuation coefficients / μ very different for bone and muscle
(very) different amounts (of X-rays) absorbed so good contrast or (very) different intensities transmitted so good contrast
or (linear) attenuation coefficients / μ similar for blood and muscle
similar amounts (of X-rays) absorbed so poor contrast or similar intensities transmitted so poor contrast
